newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA TOURISM BOOM CONTINUES DESPITE OBSTACLES.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA TOURISM BOOM CONTINUES DESPITE OBSTACLES.

text.p: South Africa's rampant crime wave and a severe lack of funds to promote tourism did little to deter foreign visitors from continuing to arrive in record numbers last year.
According to the latest annual report of the South African Tourism Board (Satour), close to five million tourists visited the country in 1996 representing a 10.2 percent rise from the previous year.
The number of overseas visitors increased by 9.4 percent to 1.17 million while visitors from Africa rose by 9.6 percent to 3.31 million.
A Satour spokeswoman told Reuters that these increases were lower than the phenomenal growth recorded in the previous year.
But this was mainly because South Africa hosted the Rugby World Cup in 1995 and was still a curiosity following its first democatic elections in 1994.

Two-thirds of all overseas arrivals in 1996 came from Europe, mainly from Britain and Germany, and they tended to be big spenders. Visitors from Africa and the Middle East contributed only 22 percent of the foreign exchange generated by tourism.
South Africa has also become increasingly attactive as a conference venue, indicating continued international confidence in and goodwill towards the country, Satour said.
"It also speaks volumes about the perceptions of the quality of South African tourist facilities, services and attractions."
"Clearly, the flavour-of-the-month status has prevailed, keeping the window of opportunity open for the growth of the industry," it said.
